title: Recipe Schema v1 (development)
description: Working schema for the fermentation/recipe widget framework. Development draft — expect changes as more recipe types are tested. Core rule: only title, ingredients and steps are required. Every other field is optional and should be OMITTED entirely (never null, empty string, or 'n/a') when it doesn't apply to a given recipe.

description.description: Short intro / tagline paragraph, as usually seen under a recipe title.

alternateNames.description: Native-language name, transliteration, or other alternate titles, e.g. ['양배추 김치', 'Yangbaechu Kimchi'].

times.description: Flexible labelled list — prep/cook/oven temps/whatever the recipe actually has. No fixed keys; omit entirely if a recipe has no meaningful timing info.

equipment.description: Only include as a list when 2+ distinct tools are worth flagging up front (e.g. shaker, jigger). A single passing tool mention should just stay in the step text instead.

steps.description: One flat, ordered array — authored in the sequence the source recipe naturally describes. Do not build a dependency graph; use 'after' only for genuine hard dependencies.

fermentationTracker.description: Only for genuine ferments (kimchi, sauerkraut, pickles). Most recipes should use a 'Storage'-labelled entry in notes instead — do not add a tracker just because something keeps for a few days.

variations.description: Named alternative versions of the recipe (e.g. 'Traditional', 'Orchard'). Distinct from notes — has its own identity in most published recipes.

notes.description: Numbered/labelled list of standalone notes — storage, flavour profile, make-ahead tips, ad-hoc yield guidance, or anything else that doesn't have its own dedicated field. This is the general-purpose catch-all for the 80/20 long tail.

adaptedBy.description: Person who adapted this version, if different from the author.

note.description: e.g. 'today, with easy repeat for 2 more tomorrow'.

unit.description: Free text — 'litres', 'jar', 'pitcher', 'batch'. Not restricted to a fixed unit list.

amount.description: Omit for free-text/to-taste items with no real quantity.

scaleMode.description: Free-form hint for the shell's scaling display logic (e.g. 'weight', 'volume', 'whole', 'whole_range'). Not a strict enum — apply common sense, don't over-engineer new modes.

display.description: Optional override string for cases where scaled math alone reads badly, e.g. '7-8 cloves'.

id.description: Optional stable id, mainly needed if another step references this one via 'after'.

component.description: Light display-only tag for grouping in the UI (e.g. 'sauce', 'potatoes'). Never affects execution order.

elapsedMinutes.description: For oven-timeline style steps keyed to elapsed time rather than pure sequence.

after.description: Id of a step this one has a genuine hard dependency on. Rare — use only when order truly matters, not as a default.

label.description: Always name the THING, not the action — e.g. 'Roast Jersey Royals', not 'Oven'. Critical when a recipe has multiple concurrent timers.

stages.description: 2-4 stages typical (e.g. too early / peak / past peak / avoid). Day thresholds are per-recipe data, not hardcoded in the shell.

toDay.description: Omit on the final stage for an open-ended range.

colour.description: e.g. 'yellow', 'green', 'amber', 'red'. Avoid red unless genuinely past sensible eating, not just past peak.
